result.notes:
SCOPE CONFLICT (needs a decision) — ysu_topdown_pblmix is domain-independent in WRF: the Registry dimension column is "1" (scalar), not max_domains (Registry.EM_COMMON:2471). gpuwm already agrees: it is a plain RunConfig field (gpuwm/config.py:117) and is deliberately absent from _DOMAIN_RUN_OVERRIDES (gpuwm/experiment.py:119), so a [[domain]] table cannot override it. But the pbl component in physics_registry_v2.json declares "scope":"per-domain". If ysu_topdown_pblmix is added under the pbl component's parameters, a per-domain override would validate and then be silently ignored by the runtime. Either declare it as a run-scoped parameter or document root-value-only semantics.

bl_pbl_physics is ALREADY in the registry, just not in the `parameters` map — it is the pbl component's selector_keys entry and the selector on the off/ysu/mynn options. I marked already_declared=true to prevent a duplicate `parameters` entry; the proposed_spec is only what it would be if the caller decides selectors also need value specs. Do not duplicate it.

REGISTRY/CODE INCONSISTENCY (belongs to the MYNN owner, flagging it because it lives in my component): the pbl component advertises an "mynn" option with selector bl_pbl_physics=5, implemented=false. gpuwm/config.py:325 hard-rejects anything outside {0,1}, so a plan naming mynn dies at RunConfig construction rather than at registry validation, and gpuwm/physics_compat.py:226 has a separate sfclay==5 or pbl==5 receipt path. The registry enum for gpuwm's actual accepted set is [0,1].

bldt: the existing spec is {"minimum":0.0,"type":"number"} with no default. WRF default is 0 (= call every step) and gpuwm's RunConfig default is 0.0, so adding "default": 0.0 is a pure documentation fix. Units are WRF minutes on both sides (gpuwm/core/physics.py:674 converts via _physics_interval_seconds; gpuwm/experiment.py:998 uses Fraction(run.bldt) * 60). Unlike radt there is no duplicate "bldt_minutes" spelling.

km_opt <-> PBL cross-constraint is already encoded and correct: the pbl "off" option carries constraints.forbidden_setting_values {"km_opt":[4]}, matching gpuwm/config.py:462 and gpuwm/core/dycore.py:1563 (km_opt=4 with bl_pbl_physics=0 raises NotImplementedError). No new PBL-side work needed. The only gap is that the km_opt parameter spec is bare {"type":"integer"} while gpuwm accepts only {1,4} (gpuwm/config.py:445, gpuwm/core/dycore.py:1555) — that tightening is the dynamics lane's call, as is whether khdif/kvdif get declared at all. There is a second cross-constraint the registry does NOT encode: km_opt=4 forbids khdif>0 or kvdif>0 (gpuwm/config.py:457).

RECOMMENDATION on topo_wind and icloud_bl: I supplied enum-of-one specs only because proposed_spec is a required field. Do not actually declare them as parameters — an enum containing a single "off" value is a pinned placeholder, and the registry already expresses unimplemented behavior through component options with implemented=false and through option-level forbidden_setting_values. If they must be visible, express them as constraints on the ysu option, not as parameters. Also note topo_wind is arguably a surface_layer knob, not a PBL knob: WRF applies it in the sfclay scheme's ctopo/ctopo2 wind correction, keyed off sub-grid orography statics, not inside YSU.

brcr_ub is confirmed on both sides: no rconfig in the corpus, and gpuwm hard-codes it at gpuwm/core/kernels/ysu.cu:110 as `const real brcr_ub = 0.0f, brcr_sb = 0.25f, cori = 1.0e-4f;` with the CPU reference mirroring it at gpuwm/verify/npref.py:6221. Declaring it would create a knob WRF itself does not expose.

Minor corpus note: Registry.CONVERT:282-283 also carries bl_pbl_physics and BLDT, both with default 0. Registry.EM_COMMON is the ARW authority and is what I cited (bl_pbl_physics default -1 there, meaning "resolve at init").

result.notes:
SELECTOR NUMBERING — no discrepancy. gpuwm's 91 for classic MM5 is WRF's own numbering, not a gpuwm invention: Registry.EM_COMMON:3137 `package sfclayscheme sf_sfclay_physics==91` and :3129 `package sfclayrevscheme sf_sfclay_physics==1`. WRF's full selector set is 0,1,2,3,4,5,7,10,89,91 (Registry.EM_COMMON:3128-3137); gpuwm accepts {0,1,91} (gpuwm/config.py:310-314), which is why the proposed enum is narrower than WRF's.

DEFAULT DIVERGENCE on sf_sfclay_physics. WRF's Registry default is -1 (a fail-closed sentinel). I propose default 0 because that is RunConfig's actual default (gpuwm/config.py:107) and 0 is a legal gpuwm value (surface layer off). gpuwm's namelist importer separately refuses to accept a missing key and will not silently disable the scheme (gpuwm/namelist_import.py:912-917). If you would rather the registry default mirror WRF, omit "default" entirely rather than encoding -1, which validate_run_config rejects.

PER-DOMAIN SCOPE. sf_sfclay_physics is max_domains in WRF, and physics_registry_v2.json already declares the surface_layer component scope "per-domain" with selector_keys ["sf_sfclay_physics"] — but gpuwm's namelist importer collapses it with _uniform() (gpuwm/namelist_import.py:918-919), i.e. one value for all domains. isftcflx, iz0tlnd, isfflx, shalwater_depth and scm_force_flux are dimension "1" (scalar/global) in WRF; shalwater_z0 and topo_wind are max_domains. Do not declare the scalar ones per-domain — that would exceed WRF.

ALREADY-A-SELECTOR. sf_sfclay_physics is currently a selector_key of the surface_layer component but is NOT in the registry's flat "parameters" dict, which is consistent with the brief's claim that it is undeclared. Adding it to "parameters" duplicates the name in two roles; confirm that is intended before landing, or the registry validator may double-bind it.

CHEAPEST REAL WIN. isftcflx and iz0tlnd are the only two knobs here that are fully coded and completely unreachable. The CUDA kernel implements every branch (sfclay.cu:356, :371, :399-402, :429), the Python wrapper validates {0,1,2} for both (gpuwm/core/sfclay.py:77-83), and the float64 verification mirror already covers them (gpuwm/verify/npref.py:4318-4319, :4517-4560, :4642-4645). The single break in the chain is gpuwm/core/physics.py:1103-1109, which passes only option= and dx=. Two RunConfig fields plus three kwargs at that one call site makes isftcflx, iz0tlnd and isfflx live. Nothing else in this component is close.

ENUM POLICY FOR UNIMPLEMENTED KNOBS. For shalwater_z0, scm_force_flux and topo_wind I proposed enum [<no-op value>] so the registry fails closed on any non-default request, matching how namelist_import treats other unsupported keys. If you prefer unimplemented knobs to be omitted from the registry entirely rather than pinned, drop those three rows — I did not want to leave them silently absent given the brief asked for missed knobs.

DELIBERATE EXCLUSIONS (found in the corpus, judged not surface-layer): ifsnow (Registry.EM_COMMON:2497, LSM snow switch; gpuwm drops it at namelist_import.py:956), seaice_threshold (:2556), fractional_seaice (:2631) and the seaice_* family, sf_ocean_physics/omlcall/oml_*/OMDT (:2613-2623, ocean mixed layer), tke_heat_flux and tke_drag_coefficient (:2900-2901, namelist,dynamics — these are the idealized-LES surface flux pair that pairs with isfflx=2 and belong to the diffusion/km_opt component), sf_urban_physics (:2486). MYNN surface layer (sf_sfclay_physics==5, Registry.EM_COMMON:3133) excluded per scope.

REGISTRY-FILE CAVEAT. Registry.CONVERT also defines sf_sfclay_physics (line 280, default 0) and packages only 91/2/3 (lines 486-488). That is the convert_em utility's registry, not wrf.exe's. Registry.EM_COMMON is the authority I cited throughout.

result.notes:
SCOPE/DECLARATION STATUS
- Registry today declares 5 radiation-adjacent parameters: icloud, ra_physics, radt, radt_minutes, wrf_rrtmg_compatibility. ra_lw_physics and ra_sw_physics appear ONLY as component selector_keys/selectors, not in the top-level "parameters" block — so they are undeclared as parameters and need declaring. swrad_scat is implemented but wholly undeclared.
- All five already-declared specs are under-constrained versus gpuwm's real accepted sets. Concretely: ra_physics has no enum (gpuwm accepts only {0,4,90}, gpuwm/config.py:335); wrf_rrtmg_compatibility has no enum (gpuwm accepts only "none" and "wrf-rrtmg-4-4-to-rte-rrtmgp-v1", gpuwm/config.py:360-365, token defined gpuwm/physics_compat.py:26); icloud/radt/radt_minutes lack defaults. My proposed_spec entries tighten these.

TWO CONTRADICTIONS THE CALLER MUST DECIDE
1. WRF dimension vs registry scope. icloud, swrad_scat, swint_opt, aer_opt and o3input are all dimension "1" (SCALAR) in Registry.EM_COMMON — one value for the whole run, not per-domain. The registry's radiation component is declared "scope":"per-domain". radt, ra_lw_physics, ra_sw_physics, slope_rad and topo_shading ARE max_domains. If per-domain overrides of icloud/swrad_scat are permitted in the experiment schema, gpuwm diverges from WRF namelist semantics for those two.
2. ra_lw_physics=1 is accepted by validation but is not executable. gpuwm/config.py:341-344 admits lw=1, and physics.py:1384-1388 then raises NotImplementedError ("WRF RRTM ... 16-band/140-g-point coefficient and transfer kernels are still required"). The proposed enum [-1,0,1,4,90] preserves that late-fail behavior; if the caller prefers fail-at-config, drop 1 from ra_lw_physics and rely on the registry option "wrf-rrtm-dudhia" (implemented=false) to carry the port-in-progress signal. Note that ra_sw_physics=1 is only executable paired with ra_lw_physics=0 (physics.py:1378), a pair constraint the flat parameter enum cannot express — it belongs in the component option table, where it already exists as "dudhia-shortwave".

result.notes:
RECOMMENDED ACTION: declare exactly ONE new parameter for this component -- cu_physics {"type":"integer","enum":[0,1],"default":0}. cudt_minutes is already correctly declared. Every other knob in this component is unimplemented and should be left out of the registry until its plumbing exists, because declaring an enum of one value advertises a control that cannot change a result.

1. TWO CANDIDATES WERE MISFILED. (a) ishallow is a Grell-3 knob, not a KF knob -- the Registry text is explicit: "shallow convection in G3 scheme". It has no effect at cu_physics=1. KF-Eta's shallow branch in gpuwm is unconditional and internal (kf.cu:594-601 promotes a failed deep candidate; kf.cu:1211 writes shallow_out). Whoever built the candidate list appears to have pattern-matched "shallow convection" to KF. (b) kfeta_trigger has Registry dimension 1, i.e. it is SCALAR, not per-domain -- unlike cu_physics and cudt, which are max_domains. If it is ever ported it must be a run-level key, not a [[domain]] override. gpuwm's per-domain override tuple (gpuwm/experiment.py:118-121) currently carries cu_physics and cudt_minutes, which is correct.

2. FOUR KF-APPLICABLE NAMELIST KNOBS THE CANDIDATE LIST MISSED: kf_edrates (Registry.EM_COMMON:2491, per-domain, "output entrainment/detrainment rates and convective timescale for KF schemes"), cu_diag (:2490, per-domain, t-averaged cumulus diagnostics), shallowcu_forced_ra (:2602, per-domain, "force radiative impact of shallow Cu (KF-Eta and KF-CuP)" -- names KF-Eta explicitly), and shcu_physics (:2489, per-domain, the independent shallow-cumulus selector). kf_edrates and cu_diag are diagnostic-only and cannot change the integration; shallowcu_forced_ra is strictly downstream of the cu_rad_feedback plumbing.

3. cu_rad_feedback RADIATION COUPLING -- what it actually needs, in order:
   (a) Kernel producer. gpuwm/core/kernels/kf.cu computes updraft liquid/ice internally but launch_kf's output dict (gpuwm/core/kf.py:143-157) exports only tendencies plus rainc/triggered/cape/timec/nca_seconds/shallow/cloud_base/cloud_top/mass fluxes. There is no QC_CU / QI_CU per-layer profile. New kernel output arrays + allocations are unavoidable.
   (b) Persistent driver state. Convective cloud must survive between cumulus calls because radt and cudt are different cadences: the cumulus block runs only on STEPCU-due steps (gpuwm/core/physics.py:1253-1273). The qc_cu/qi_cu/cldfra_cu arrays therefore need to be held across the interval exactly the way the KF rates already are, and they need VRAM slots registered in gpuwm/core/preflight.py alongside the existing "cumulus/w0avg" entry at preflight.py:461 -- non-trivial on a 29-30 GB budget, since these are full 3D fields per cumulus domain.
   (c) Radiation consumer. gpuwm/core/rrtmgp.py:1733 builds CLDFRA purely as cal_cldfra1(qv, qc, qi, qs, tlay, play) from RESOLVED hydrometeors, and rrtmgp.py:884 converts grid-box to in-cloud paths via max(0.01, cldfra). There is no merge point today. A convective-cloud merge has to happen before hydrometeor_paths and before the McICA subcolumn masks are drawn, or the optics and the overlap sampling disagree.
   (d) The derived ICLOUD_CU switch (Registry.EM_COMMON:2610, derived not namelist) is what the WRF radiation driver actually branches on; gpuwm would derive it the same way it already derives cu_used at gpuwm/core/nssl2_runtime.py:433.
   Bottom line: cu_rad_feedback is not a wiring job, it is a KF-kernel-output + radiation-input-path change with a real VRAM cost. It should stay undeclared until that work is scoped.

4. NAME COLLISION WARNING FOR THE REGISTRY: the WRF namelist spelling is cudt (minutes); gpuwm's RunConfig field is cudt_minutes. The translation happens in gpuwm/namelist_import.py:943 (reads cudt) and :1296 (emits cudt_minutes), and :1297-1299 drops a nonzero cudt on any domain where cu_physics != 1. Keep the registry name as cudt_minutes; do not introduce a second cudt alias.

5. gpuwm's accepted cu_physics set is {0, 1}, enforced in two independent places -- gpuwm/config.py:375-378 and gpuwm/core/physics.py:1356-1357 -- with the namelist importer's _CU_ALLOWED = {0, 1} at gpuwm/namelist_import.py:243. So the registry enum is [0, 1], NOT WRF's full option list. Also note WRF's Registry default for cu_physics is -1 (a deliberate must-set sentinel; the importer rejects it explicitly at namelist_import.py:932-936). Do not propagate -1 as the registry default -- use gpuwm's own default of 0.

6. Two cumulus-adjacent knobs I deliberately did NOT make rows, to avoid poaching another component: prec_acc_dt (Registry.EM_COMMON:2643, per-domain real, minutes, "bucket reset time interval between outputs for cumulus or grid scale precipitation") is a shared precip-bucket OUTPUT knob spanning cumulus and microphysics; and convtrans_avglen_m (:2547, scalar real, default 30) is the averaging window that only matters once cu_diag exists. Also excluded: the KF-CuP PDF knobs numBins/thBinSize/rBinSize/minDeepFreq/minShallowFreq/shcu_aerosols_opt (:2603-2608) and the Grell ensemble knobs maxiens/maxens/maxens2/maxens3/ensdim/cugd_avedx/clos_choice/imomentum (:2538-2546) -- all belong to cumulus schemes gpuwm does not implement.

7. Scope note: I did not touch MYNN, Noah-MP, or RUC LSM.

HAZARD -- mp_tend_lim bound: validate_run_config requires strictly > 0 and finite (gpuwm/config.py:427). The registry's "minimum" is inclusive, so a declared minimum of 0 would admit 0.0 at registry level and then fail at config validation. Accept the mismatch or pick a small positive minimum -- caller's call.

NSSL SUMMARY: none of the twelve NSSL candidates is a RunConfig field or an experiment-schema key. gpuwm/core/nssl2_contract.py is a CPU-only frozen contract; resolve_nssl2_mode() is called exactly once with WRF defaults (line 167) and its only non-test consumers are restart-receipt provenance dumps (gpuwm/io/restart.py:414-415). So even WRF cannot vary most of the NSSL mode per nest. result.notes:
SCOPE RESULT: all 32 RunConfig fields in this component are implemented (a consuming read exists outside config.py for every one). 8 are already declared (epssm, km_opt, diff_6th_opt, diff_6th_factor, diff_6th_slopeopt, spec_exp, terrain_opt, top_lid); 24 need declaration. Of the 4 experiment-schema keys, blend_width and p_top are implemented; feedback and smooth_option are parsed-but-fail-closed at nonzero.

PER-DOMAIN vs SCALAR (WRF dimension column, the authority):
- max_domains (per-domain): time_step_sound, epssm, smdiv, emdiv, khdif, kvdif, c_s, km_opt, zdamp, dampcoef, diff_6th_opt, diff_6th_factor, diff_6th_slopeopt, diff_6th_thresh, h_sca_adv_order, top_lid, specified, nested, open_xs/open_xe/open_ys/open_ye, map_proj.
- scalar (dimension "1"): damp_opt, w_damping, hybrid_opt, etac, base_temp, hypsometric_opt, spec_bdy_width, spec_zone, relax_zone, spec_exp, feedback, smooth_option, blend_width, p_top_requested.
Note the WRF asymmetry: damp_opt/w_damping are SCALAR while zdamp/dampcoef are per-domain; spec_zone/relax_zone/spec_bdy_width are SCALAR while specified/nested are per-domain. gpuwm's RunConfig is already per-domain for all of them, which is a superset of WRF and is safe, but the registry scope metadata should not claim WRF per-domain-ness for the scalar ones.

NOT WRF NAMELIST KNOBS (2 of 34):
- terrain_opt: no rconfig anywhere in the 39-file corpus. It is a gpuwm-only selector (0 = flat idealized profile columns, nonzero = real 3-D terrain / bell hill). Already declared. Keep it, but the registry should not imply WRF provenance.
- map_proj: an rconfig exists (Registry.EM_COMMON:2988, Registry.CONVERT:377) but its section column is "derived", NOT "namelist,*" -- WRF derives it from the wrfinput/WPS metadata, so it is not a namelist.input knob.

NAME DIVERGENCES the caller must decide on:
- gpuwm open_x / open_y collapse WRF's four independent per-edge logicals open_xs, open_xe, open_ys, open_ye (Registry.EM_COMMON:2934/2935/2939/2940). A gpuwm open_x=true means BOTH x edges radiative. If per-edge control is ever needed the registry name must change, so declaring open_x/open_y now locks in the collapsed semantics.
- experiment key p_top vs WRF p_top_requested. Recommend keeping the gpuwm spelling and recording the WRF alias in the description, not renaming.

VALUE-SET DIVERGENCES from WRF (gpuwm is far more restrictive):
- km_opt: WRF allows 0/1/2/3; gpuwm accepts ONLY {1,4} (config.py:445). Note gpuwm's "4" is WRF diff_opt=2 2-D Smagorinsky, not WRF km_opt=4.
- hypsometric_opt: gpuwm {1,2}, default 1 (WRF default 2).
- h_sca_adv_order: WRF allows 2..6; gpuwm accepts ONLY {2,5} (config.py:480), default 2 (WRF 5).
- diff_6th_slopeopt: gpuwm {0,1} (config.py:470).
- map_proj: gpuwm {0,1} (config.py:295); Lambert only.
- hybrid_opt: gpuwm {0,1,2}, default 0 (WRF default 2).
- diff_6th_opt: no explicit membership check in validate_run_config; the kernel treats mono==2 as monotonic and anything else as plain (gpuwm/core/kernels/diff6.cu:91). config.py:518 forbids diff_6th_opt=1 with moist=true. Proposed enum [0,1,2] reflects the actual implemented branches.

FAIL-OPEN GAPS FOUND (registry declaration would close them; each is a real hole today):
1. damp_opt has NO validation anywhere. Only damp_opt==3 does anything (gpuwm/core/acoustic.py:320, gpuwm/core/diffusion.py:145); damp_opt=1 or 2 is accepted and SILENTLY does nothing -- a user porting a WRF namelist with damp_opt=2 gets an undamped model top with no warning. Proposed enum [0,3] closes it, but it is a behavior-visible tightening, so the caller must sign off.
2. w_damping has no validation; only ==1 acts (gpuwm/core/dycore.py:1400). Same silent-noop shape.
3. time_step_sound=0 (WRF's "auto" default) passes the even-parity check at config.py:275 and then divides by zero at gpuwm/core/dycore.py:1666-1667 (cfg.dt / ns). Proposed minimum 2 fixes it. If the registry ever ingests a raw WRF namelist, 0 is the DEFAULT value there, so this is likely to be hit.
4. terrain_opt is read as truthy/falsy everywhere (state.py:479 `== 0`, nest_init.py:654 `not cfg.terrain_opt`), so any nonzero int is accepted. Proposed enum [0,1] is a tightening.
5. epssm, smdiv, emdiv, dampcoef, diff_6th_factor, zdamp, base_temp have no finiteness/range validation in validate_run_config. The proposed minimum/maximum bounds are tightenings, not descriptions of today's accepted set. diff_6th_factor's [0,1] bound IS enforced but only on the clock-scaled path (gpuwm/core/dycore.py:1094).

MAP_PROJ CAVEAT (be aware before declaring): cfg.map_proj is never read by the dycore. Grep for map_proj across gpuwm/core returns only a comment in kernels/coriolis_map.cu. The only consuming read of the RunConfig/experiment value is gpuwm/experiment.py:721-731, which enforces "map_proj == 1 <=> a [projection] table exists". Actual map factors and Coriolis reach the dycore through DomainState.msft/msfu/msfv/f/e via set_map_coriolis (gpuwm/runtime.py:475), driven by the [projection] table, not by this integer. I marked it implemented=true on the strength of that experiment.py read, but it is a schema-coupling selector rather than a physics switch -- flag if the caller's implemented=true bar means "changes numerics".

CROSS-FIELD CONSTRAINTS NOT EXPRESSIBLE in the spec vocabulary (type/enum/minimum/maximum/default only) -- these must stay in validate_run_config, and declaring the parameters must not be read as replacing them:
- time_step_sound must be EVEN (config.py:275).
- spec_bdy_width >= spec_zone + relax_zone (config.py:495, mirrored at experiment.py:734).
- km_opt=4 forbids khdif/kvdif > 0 (config.py:457) and requires bl_pbl_physics != 0 (config.py:462, NotImplementedError).
- h_sca_adv_order=5 forbids open_x/open_y (config.py:486).
- terrain_opt != 0 forbids open_x/open_y (config.py:502).
- khdif/kvdif > 0 forbids open_x/open_y/specified (config.py:510).
- diff_6th_opt=1 forbids moist=true (config.py:518).
- diff_6th_thresh must be strictly > 0 (config.py:475); the vocabulary has no exclusiveMinimum, so minimum 0.0 is the closest expressible bound.
- specified and nested are mutually exclusive (enforced by the experiment loader, not by validate_run_config).

DEFAULTS THAT DIVERGE FROM WRF (deliberate, documented in config.py; do not "fix" them by copying WRF's registry default into the spec):
emdiv 0.0 vs 0.01; h_sca_adv_order 2 vs 5; hybrid_opt 0 vs 2; hypsometric_opt 1 vs 2; damp_opt 0 vs 3; km_opt 1 vs -1; top_lid true vs .false. (config.py:156-164 documents a stability receipt for the rigid-lid default); time_step_sound 4 vs 0.

result.notes:
SPEC CONVENTION USED. For knobs gpuwm cannot honor I proposed a single-value fail-closed enum pinned to gpuwm's current frozen behavior (e.g. tmn_update enum [0], ua_phys enum [false], rdmaxalb enum [true]) so a plan cannot silently request unported physics. For the three trivial-wire Noah knobs whose kernel branches ALREADY exist (usemonalb, rdlai2d, opt_thcnd) I proposed the post-wiring spec (both/all supported values). If the caller declares those BEFORE wiring the launch_noah pass-through, the enums must be temporarily pinned to [false], [false] and [1] respectively, otherwise the registry will accept a value the runtime silently ignores.

sf_surface_physics IS ALREADY IN THE REGISTRY, but as a component selector, not a top-level parameter: physics_registry_v2.json land_surface.selector_keys = ["sf_surface_physics"] with four options (off=0, noah=2, ruc-lsm=3 implemented:false, noah-mp=4 implemented:false). physics_registry.py skips selector keys when validating expert settings (`if name in selector_owners: continue`), so adding sf_surface_physics to the top-level "parameters" map would be redundant and could conflict with the ruc/noah-mp option selectors. I marked it already-declared; the caller should decide whether a duplicate parameter entry is wanted. Note the enum I give ([0,2]) is gpuwm's actual accepted set per validate_run_config (gpuwm/config.py:315-319) and is NARROWER than the registry's four declared options.

num_soil_layers TIGHTENING WARNING. Its current spec is {"type":"integer","minimum":1}, but gpuwm/config.py:320-324 accepts only 4. I propose enum [4]. Option-level "parameters" bypass spec validation (physics_registry.py:877-881 does a plain settings.update), so the ruc-lsm option's declared num_soil_layers=9 will NOT be rejected by enum [4]; only a user-supplied domain parameter of 9 would be, which is the correct fail-closed behavior since RUC is implemented:false. Also note the WRF Registry dimension column for num_soil_layers is "1" (scalar), i.e. it is NOT per-domain in WRF, even though gpuwm treats land_surface as scope "per-domain".

WEAK IMPLEMENTATION CLAIM. num_soil_layers is a RunConfig field read outside config.py (gpuwm/physics_compat.py:246, reached via gpuwm/config.py:303-309), but that read is only a fail-closed readiness selector - it never sizes anything. The soil dimension is hardcoded 4 in the launcher (gpuwm/core/noah.py:397-398 raises "Noah port is fixed at 4 soil layers") and in the layer-thickness constant NOAH_LAYER_THICKNESS_M. I still reported gpuwm_implemented=true because it meets the stated criterion, but the caller should know it is a gate, not a knob.

PER-DOMAIN TRUTH. Only sf_surface_physics has dimension max_domains. Every other knob in this table has dimension "1" (scalar/global) in WRF: num_soil_layers, usemonalb, rdlai2d, rdmaxalb, ua_phys, opt_thcnd, tmn_update, all seaice_*, fractional_seaice, surface_input_source, num_land_cat, num_soil_cat, sst_update, ifsnow, sf_surface_mosaic. If they are declared as per-domain parameters under a "per-domain" component scope, gpuwm will be strictly more expressive than WRF and a multi-domain plan could produce a configuration WRF cannot represent.

xice_threshold IS NOT A NAMELIST KNOB. I grepped the whole 39-file corpus for xice_threshold and found zero rconfig hits. In WRF it is derived from fractional_seaice (0.5 when off, 0.02 when on); gpuwm reproduces exactly that derivation at gpuwm/core/landuse.py:180 and takes it as a launcher kwarg at gpuwm/core/noah.py:379. Do not declare it.

CROSS-COMPONENT / OUT OF MY SCOPE. isfflx (Registry.EM_COMMON:2496, integer, dim 1, default 1) gates surface heat/moisture fluxes and is handled by gpuwm/namelist_import.py:946-954 (hard-rejects anything but 1). I did not include it in the table because it belongs to the surface_layer component; flag it to whoever owns sf_sfclay_physics. iz0tlnd (:2625) is likewise surface-layer. flag_sm_adj (:2537) is explicitly RUC-only per its Registry description and belongs to the excluded agent. mosaic_lu (:2535) and mosaic_soil (:2536) are subordinate to sf_surface_mosaic and are also hard-rejected nonzero at gpuwm/namelist_import.py:971-975; add them only if sf_surface_mosaic is declared.

REGISTRY.CONVERT DIVERGENCE. Registry.CONVERT gives different defaults for the same names (sf_surface_physics default 0 at :281 vs -1 at :2468 in Registry.EM_COMMON; num_land_cat 24 at :299 vs 21 at :2548). Registry.EM_COMMON is the ARW model build; I used it as the authority throughout and cited CONVERT only where it disagrees.

VERIFY-MIRROR HITS ARE NOT CONSUMING READS. gpuwm/verify/npref.py contains usemonalb/rdlai2d/opt_thcnd as parameters of the float64 Noah mirror (e.g. :5616, :5938-5939). Those are reference-implementation arguments with the same pinned defaults, not runtime configuration reads, so I did not count them.
